mapping.author: Forma
mapping.method: Each inventory record was reviewed against its historical category and study metadata, then assigned manually to one or more task-oriented cases authored for Forma. Case descriptions start from implementation questions and acceptance checks; they are not descriptions of the referenced websites. No upstream descriptive paragraphs, ratings, mood labels or screenshots are included.
limits: Every assignment is a research hypothesis derived from historical metadata, not a verified statement about the current website or its implementation.
No website was revisited or captured for this index. Availability, current appearance, interactions, underlying technologies and mobile behavior remain unverified.
A case lists questions to investigate and adaptations to test; it does not assert that a candidate website already implements, passes or permits any of them.
The 202 external candidates may share cases. They are neither 202 distinct implementation problems nor Forma-owned designs.
Names and URLs preserve attribution to the external destinations. This index grants no permission to copy website code, branding, images, fonts or other assets.
Before implementation, inspect only the selected candidates on the target viewports, record date and state, and validate the resulting implementation independently.

cases.name: Extended reading and report navigation
cases.whenToUse: Use when an essay, research report, documentation page or cultural story must remain readable through several chapters and screen sizes.
questions: What should a reader understand before following the next link?
Which headings need stable URLs, a contents list or return-to-reading behavior?
adapt: Build the heading hierarchy and reading width with the project’s real text before adding decorative media.
Keep chapter navigation separate from content; retain the reading position when opening a citation or returning from a detail.
verify: Test long headings, text zoom, a narrow viewport and keyboard navigation without loss of reading order.
Check that citations remain reachable when motion and background media are disabled.

cases.name: Type specimen and expressive text
cases.whenToUse: Use for typography, fonts, typefaces, large labels, wordmarks and text-led interfaces whose hierarchy depends on actual character metrics.
questions: Which text is information, and which text is a brand asset?
How do font loading, alternate languages and long names change the intended composition?
adapt: Choose a type scale from the content hierarchy; give display text and controls different wrapping constraints.
Keep essential text selectable and readable; test the fallback font before adding font-dependent motion.
verify: Inspect clipping, line breaks and baseline alignment at desktop and phone widths.
Confirm that a font failure, 200% text scaling and reduced motion leave all labels usable.

cases.name: Browse projects without losing context
cases.whenToUse: Use for a portfolio, work archive, image gallery or project index where a visitor alternates between a collection and one selected item.
questions: What information is required to choose a project without opening every item?
Does back navigation restore the previous selection, filter and scroll position?
adapt: Create a stable project model with IDs, titles, media and destinations, then select a grid or list for the available content.
Keep selection and ordering in state rather than deriving them from the visual position of an animated card.
verify: Open an item, return, resize and refresh; confirm the selected item and surrounding context remain understandable.
Check empty collections, missing thumbnails, long project titles and keyboard access to every item.

cases.name: Demonstrate a real software task
cases.whenToUse: Use for a SaaS, AI product, developer tool or consumer app page that must show what a control does instead of relying on a decorative mockup.
questions: Which action and observable result prove the product claim?
Is the demonstration using real functionality, an isolated fixture or a noninteractive recording?
adapt: Implement one bounded task with initial, loading, success and failure states; label fixtures and recordings accurately.
Use the existing product components where possible and prevent demo input from altering a real account.
verify: Exercise the demonstrated action with keyboard and touch and verify its result.
Test slow responses, empty input, retries and cancellation; do not imply an integration that the demo does not execute.

cases.name: Inspect a physical or 3D object
cases.whenToUse: Use when product decisions require inspecting a book, device, package, material, cover, spine or other physical object from more than one view.
questions: Which geometry and material details must be visible for the task?
Which angles, colors and text surfaces define acceptance rather than a single attractive pose?
adapt: Separate geometry, material, lighting and camera parameters so each cause can be refined independently.
Provide explicit front, side and back views, readable surface text and a useful static fallback that shares the same object data.
verify: Compare silhouette, joins, occlusion and surface readability at every required angle, including grazing views.
Test rotation with touch and keyboard, dark and light surroundings, reduced motion and unavailable WebGL.

cases.name: Navigate an interactive scene
cases.whenToUse: Use when a room, map, orbit or other spatial scene is itself the route to content rather than a background behind ordinary navigation.
questions: What objects can receive focus, and what destination or state does each expose?
What is the equivalent path when spatial rendering, pointer precision or motion is unavailable?
adapt: Model destinations independently of camera coordinates, then connect scene hotspots and a conventional list to the same IDs.
Bound camera movement and transitions; keep a visible escape route and avoid trapping page scrolling.
verify: Reach every destination with keyboard and touch and return to the prior view.
Verify loading failure, reduced motion, orientation changes and a rendering fallback without losing access to content.

cases.name: Video and photographic sequences
cases.whenToUse: Use for a showreel, artist page, hospitality film or image-led project where media selection, loading and playback affect the meaning of the page.
questions: Is this media necessary to understand the content or optional atmosphere?
Who owns the media, and what still image, caption or transcript can represent it when playback is unavailable?
adapt: Use approved media with a traceable source; set dimensions and a meaningful poster before the player loads.
Design play, pause, mute and still-image states and keep overlay text readable independently of the current frame.
verify: Test autoplay rejection, a failed media request, slow loading and offscreen playback behavior.
Check keyboard controls, captions when required, contrast over changing frames and reduced-motion treatment.

cases.name: Character and mascot as interface feedback
cases.whenToUse: Use when a character, mascot, avatar or illustrated guide communicates a product identity or responds to an interaction.
questions: Which recognizable features must remain stable across poses and sizes?
Does each expression communicate a state, or is it purely decorative?
adapt: Define silhouette, proportions, facial anchors and a small set of intentional expressions before refining material or motion.
Separate personality animation from functional status; expose errors and progress in ordinary text as well.
verify: Compare the character at avatar size, full size and all supported themes.
Verify interrupted transitions, reduced motion and failure states without misleading emotional or progress cues.

cases.name: Translate identity into reusable UI roles
cases.whenToUse: Use when a brand’s color, shape or visual motif needs to support buttons, sections, content and navigation across several pages.
questions: Which attributes identify the brand, and which controls must remain conventional for comprehension?
Can the same visual roles work with real content in light and dark modes?
adapt: Create separate tokens for text, surface, border, action and status before assigning decorative colors.
Apply the motif to a small reusable set of components; preserve labels, focus indication and a clear primary action.
verify: Review hover, focus, selected, disabled and error states in both themes.
Check contrast and information hierarchy with the decorative motif removed and with color perception differences.

cases.name: Restaurant, cafe and destination booking forms
cases.whenToUse: Use for a restaurant, coffee shop, cafe, hotel or destination page where a booking form supports reserving or checking availability alongside practical visit information.
questions: Can a visitor quickly find location, opening times, accessible contact and booking conditions?
Which date, party size or accommodation constraints must be checked before a reservation can succeed?
adapt: Place practical visit information alongside the relevant action; use current verified content rather than decorative sample details.
Preserve entered dates and guest details across validation or provider failures, and distinguish an enquiry from a confirmed booking.
verify: Complete the booking or enquiry path on a narrow screen and verify the confirmation state.
Test unavailable dates, invalid party size, external-provider failure and a visitor who cannot use a map.

cases.name: Event agenda and registration forms
cases.whenToUse: Use for a conference, festival, talk, invitation or recurring event with sessions, participants and a registration form.
questions: Which date, time zone, venue and admission conditions must be visible before registration?
How will visitors compare sessions and recover their place in the schedule?
adapt: Use structured event and session data for the agenda and any calendar export; make sold-out and changed sessions explicit.
Keep registration and payment boundaries understandable and preserve the attendee’s draft when validation fails.
verify: Check time-zone display, session overlaps, agenda navigation and mobile registration.
Verify empty and sold-out states, expired links and the difference between submitted interest and a confirmed place.

cases.name: Find and compare items in a collection
cases.whenToUse: Use for an archive, product catalogue, reference library, icon collection or saved-item app that requires search, filters or comparison.
questions: Which facets and metadata help a user narrow the collection without guessing?
What identifies an item when its image, ordering or display label changes?
adapt: Define stable IDs and explicit filter scope, then keep query, selection and visible results synchronized.
Provide a list alternative to unusual visual arrangements and explain a genuine empty result without replacing it with unrelated items.
verify: Test combined filters, duplicate labels, missing media, long queries and back navigation.
Verify keyboard and touch selection and ensure late responses cannot replace results for a newer query.

cases.name: Explain metrics, flows and relationships
cases.whenToUse: Use when a report, finance product, timeline, map or operational view must explain numbers, connections or process status.
questions: What dataset, units, period and source support each visible claim?
Does a line represent a measured relationship, a process step or only decoration?
adapt: Keep chart, table, labels and summaries connected to one declared dataset.
Use semantic colors and explicit legends; distinguish real relationships from illustrative layouts and mark simulated values.
verify: Check totals, rounding, missing values and changes in the selected time range.
Compare the visual account against a readable table or list, including keyboard access and narrow-screen behavior.

cases.name: Live appearance controls and persistence
cases.whenToUse: Use for theme selection, color picking, lighting, typography controls or a preview panel that lets a user change a visual setting.
questions: Which value belongs to the preview draft, and when does it become the saved setting?
Which values and positions must remain unchanged when one control is edited?
adapt: Reuse the canonical control and state model; separate mode, context color, light positions and intensity instead of coupling them.
Keep save, cancel and reset behavior explicit; changing the selected object must not move unrelated objects or discard their values.
verify: Test every starting state, add and remove action, selection and reopen cycle.
Compare desktop and mobile rendering, keyboard operation, system-theme changes and saved-state restoration.

cases.name: Service proof and recoverable enquiry forms
cases.whenToUse: Use for an agency, consultancy, professional practice, architecture service or property presentation that must lead from evidence to an enquiry form.
questions: Which authentic project, qualification or service detail supports the visitor’s decision?
What is the minimum information needed to route the enquiry to the appropriate team?
adapt: Arrange the offer, relevant proof and next action around the customer’s task rather than a generic collection of visual effects.
Use a short labelled form, make any external handoff visible and preserve the draft when submission fails.
verify: Verify that claims and images belong to the service being offered and remain readable on a phone.
Exercise validation, repeated submission, confirmation and failure recovery; do not confuse a local form demo with message delivery.

cases.name: Sequential explanation driven by progress
cases.whenToUse: Use when scrolling, paging or a progress control reveals an ordered explanation, comparison or process instead of simply moving a static page.
questions: What information changes at each step, and can the sequence be understood without animation?
Can a visitor reverse, interrupt or jump into the sequence without seeing a contradictory state?
adapt: Define the sequence as explicit states with content first, then connect scroll or page progress to those states.
Keep the ordinary document order meaningful and provide reduced-motion behavior without removing the explanation.
verify: Test forward and reverse traversal, rapid input, resize and restored scroll position.
Check keyboard reading order, short viewports, content loaded late and interruption while a transition is active.
